figures.caption: Figure 2: From left to right: original flow W , symmetric component Ws from orthogonal projection, symmetric component Ws from minimal projection, skew-symmetric component Wa (orthogonal), and skew-symmetric component Wa (minimal). Green (red) edges denote positive (negative) weights.
Figure 3: The 4 × 4 toy grid used for validation. Left: directed graph with bidirectional edges (42 undirected edges). Right: triangulated 2-simplicial complex (36 oriented triangles).

Table 1: Ground-truth recovery on the fully triangulated 4 × 4 grid. The harmonic norm sits at machine precision in every case because this grid has trivial first homology; the next subsection exhibits a genuine harmonic component on a complex with a hole.

Figure 4: Hodge recovery on the fully triangulated grid. The harmonic column is empty by construction, since the harmonic subspace here is zero-dimensional. Rows: pure gradient, pure curl, mixed input. Columns: input flow Wa, recovered gradient −δ0φ̂, curl δ∗1ψ̂, and harmonic ĥ. Arrow color encodes sign (green positive, red negative) and width encodes magnitude.

Figure 5: Hodge decomposition on a 4×4 grid with the central square left un-triangulated, creating a 1-D hole. Left to right: mixed input flow (gradient + curl + hole circulation); recovered gradient; recovered curl; recovered harmonic, circulating around the hole.
Table 2: Node-level results for the detection experiment, ranked by |Tφp | (all 924 block permutations enumerated exactly). The truly perturbed node is node 5.

Figure 6: Detection of a planted hierarchical perturbation on the VAR system. Left: spatial map of ∆φ̂; the perturbed node (5, gold star) shows the largest negative shift and its four driving neighbors the largest positive shifts. Right: |Tφp | ranked by effect size.

Figure 7: Experimental setup for the ischemic stroke model (pMCAo) with LFP recordings in S1 near the MCA territory. Left: schematic of the rat during pMCAo. Middle: dorsal view of MCA territory and S1. Right: cortical slice showing electrode placement across layers.
Figure 8: Sample LFP recordings from channels 1–3 in one rat. Each trace shows a representative 1 s epoch before and after stroke. Data acquired at 1 kHz and downsampled to 250 Hz.
Figure 9: The 2-D simplicial complex for the LFP grid. Left: directed network with edges between neighboring electrodes. Right: triangular faces tiling local neighborhoods.

Figure 10: Hodge decomposition averaged across all epochs in each condition for Rat F141020. Top row: pre-pMCAo. Bottom row: post-pMCAo. Left: gradient component. Right: curl component. The harmonic component is identically zero on this fully triangulated grid (Section 3.1).
Figure 11: Node potentials averaged over 5 min pre-pMCAo (left) and 5 min post-pMCAo (right) for Rat F141020. Higher potential indicates a more source-like position in the feedforward hierarchy.

Figure 12: Normalized component energies over epochs for Rat F141020. For each 1 s epoch we compute ∥−δ0φ̂∥2F/∥Wa∥2F (Gradient, blue) and the analogous Curl ratio (orange). The harmonic component is identically zero on this fully triangulated grid (Section 3.1). The first 60 epochs precede pMCAo; the last 60 follow it.

Figure 13: Significantly affected nodes for Rat F141020 (BH-FDR q < 0.05). Color encodes ∆φ̂ (post − pre); red indicates a drop in rank, green an increase. BH-significant nodes have black borders; the top five by |T | are marked with a gold star.

Figure 14: Significantly affected triangles for Rat F141020 (BH-FDR q < 0.05). Color encodes ∆ψ̂; BH-significant patches have black outlines. The top five by |T | are highlighted in gold, with arrows indicating post-stroke circulation direction.

Table 4: Per-rat counts of BH-significant nodes and triangles (α = 0.05), with the three most-affected nodes and triangles (by |T |) for each animal. Triangles are indexed by position in the sorted list of unique triangles.
Figure 15: Per-rat spatial maps of significantly affected nodes (left) and triangles (right) for the three animals not shown in the main text. Conventions follow Figs. 13 and 14.
